raw_response:
I’m 62 now, so I don’t chase fancy changes. On 12 mu, with only two people at home, I need a plan that is steady, not troublesome, and can still give decent income. Even though cotton can bring money in a good year, it ties up labor too long and picking is hard for my age and household size. With well irrigation and so many years on this land, I would still keep the full 12 mu in the wheat-maize rotation. I know this system well, the timing is familiar, and it spreads risk across the year. For wheat, I will use a good improved variety, put most of the phosphorus and potassium plus part of the nitrogen as base fertilizer, then topdress once at jointing. I don’t want to cut fertilizer too much because wheat responds clearly on my fields, but I also won’t push it to the highest level because pumping water and fertilizer both cost money. For maize after wheat, the turnaround is tight, so I will keep tillage simple, sow quickly after harvest, and rely on one base application plus one topdress around the big flare stage. If rain is normal, one irrigation for maize is enough; if summer is dry, I can add one more from the well. My goal is stable yield with manageable cash cost and work load.
